story.title: Tenerife Footballer Jesus De Miguel Dies After On-Field Collision
story.summary: Jesus De Miguel, a 30-year-old forward for Tenerife, has died following a collision during a match. The incident occurred when he was struck in the chest while challenging for the ball, leading to a cardiac arrest. His club expressed deep sorrow over the loss.

explore_lenses.label: Why are police investigating a match incident?
explore_lenses.title: A routine legal inquiry, not a finding of guilt
explore_lenses.summary: Spanish police have opened an investigation because De Miguel's death followed a non-natural, on-field injury. The inquiry is under judicial supervision and is intended to establish the medical and factual sequence, rather than to presume criminal responsibility.

claims.text: Police opened an investigation into the circumstances of De Miguel's death; sources cited by EFE say deaths deemed non-natural, including accidental ones, automatically trigger judicial proceedings in the Canary Islands.
The precise medical cause of death had not been publicly disclosed as of November 3, despite reports that De Miguel suffered cardiac arrest after the collision.

Santa Cruz de Tenerife's chief prosecutor, José Luis Sánchez-Jáuregui, said a criminal case would be 'very difficult' because the collision occurred during play, while stressing that the referee's report and disciplinary findings must first be reviewed.

explore_lenses.label: What could happen to goalkeeper Jesús Owono?
explore_lenses.title: Sporting discipline and criminal review are separate
explore_lenses.summary: Owono's red card ensures a disciplinary review, but it does not by itself establish criminal liability. Authorities and football bodies will assess different questions: whether the challenge breached sporting rules and whether it exceeded the risks inherent in play.

claims.text: LaLiga's official match record lists Owono's red card and the abandonment of Tenerife-Andorra at 2-2; the game was stopped after the incident.
Reporting on the referee's report says Owono was sent off for striking an opponent with a raised leg and excessive force while the ball was being contested.

The prosecutor's view is that injuries during sport are generally not criminally punishable unless conduct falls outside the normal dynamics of the game, such as an intentional assault; he said disciplinary findings will be important to the assessment.
Any final sporting sanction or criminal charge remains unresolved because the disciplinary body, police inquiry and judicial process have not concluded.

explore_lenses.label: How is Spanish football responding now?
explore_lenses.title: Competitions paused as the sport mourns
explore_lenses.summary: The immediate response has extended beyond Tenerife: Spain's federation postponed scheduled cup fixtures and later widened the suspension of its own competitions. The moves reflect mourning and practical disruption, while replacement dates remain unannounced.

claims.text: The RFEF initially postponed the Copa del Rey and Copa de la Reina matches scheduled for November 3, saying the decision was a mark of respect and solidarity after De Miguel's death.
Later on November 3, the RFEF said it had expanded the suspension of its competitions to three days, through November 6.
UEFA said a minute of silence would be observed at its matches that week, according to AP.
The RFEF said it would announce revised tournament planning and definitive kickoff times in coming days.

story_report.summary: Jesús De Miguel, a 30-year-old Tenerife player in Spain’s second division, died after suffering a cardiac arrest following a collision during a match. Tenerife’s game against Andorra was stopped and recorded as abandoned at 2-2 after the incident; Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono was sent off. Spanish football authorities responded by postponing competitions as police began examining the circumstances of De Miguel’s death.

sections.heading: Investigation Into De Miguel’s Death
sections.body: Police opened an investigation into De Miguel’s death, a process sources cited by EFE said is automatically triggered in the Canary Islands when a death is considered non-natural, including accidental deaths. Reporting on the referee’s report said Owono was dismissed for striking an opponent with a raised leg and excessive force while contesting the ball. Santa Cruz de Tenerife’s chief prosecutor, José Luis Sánchez-Jáuregui, said a criminal case would be very difficult because the collision occurred during play, though he said the referee’s report and disciplinary findings must be reviewed.

sections.heading: Spanish Football Responds to Death
sections.body: The Spanish Football Federation initially postponed Copa del Rey and Copa de la Reina matches scheduled for Nov. 3, describing the move as a mark of respect and solidarity. Later that day, it extended the suspension of its competitions through Nov. 6 and said revised tournament planning and definitive kickoff times would be announced in the coming days. UEFA also said a minute’s silence would be observed at its matches that week, according to AP.

unresolved.text: The precise medical cause of De Miguel’s death, including any forensic finding on a causal connection between the collision and his death, had not been publicly disclosed as of Nov. 3.
No final disciplinary penalty or criminal charge involving Owono had been announced, as the disciplinary, police and judicial processes had not concluded.
New dates for postponed matches and the final disposition of the abandoned Tenerife-Andorra match had not been announced.

related_stories.title: Russian Airstrikes on Ukrainian Aid Center Result in 31 Deaths and Many Missing
related_stories.summary: A Russian bombing raid on a humanitarian aid center in the village of Komyshuvakha, located in southern Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region, has resulted in at least 31 fatalities. Emergency teams are searching through the debris, with more than 45 residents reported missing. The attack involved the use of large aerial bombs and is part of a broader wave of strikes across Ukraine, which also targeted power plants and hospitals.

related_stories.title: Supreme Court Considers Catholic Schools' Participation in Colorado Preschool Program
related_stories.summary: The Supreme Court is deliberating a case involving Catholic preschools in Colorado that seek to join the state's universal preschool program. The schools argue that their exclusion based on their admissions policy, which does not accept families with gay and transgender parents, is unconstitutional. The court appears to be sympathetic to the Catholic schools' position regarding potential exemptions from Colorado's anti-discrimination rules for taxpayer-funded programs.
